doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Writing his book, bebop influences and Erroll Garner
summary: Marty mentions his unpublished book, favourite pianists Peterson and Garner, and Garner's intro on 'That's My Kick'.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: So I mean these are stories that, you know when I do a club date or something and we sit in the back room, and the guys want to know these stories, they say “man, why don’t you write a book?” I say “I wrote a book, nobody wants to publish it.” I’m trying to get somebody to condense it because it’s seven million pages long.
Who were you listening to at the time? You considered yourself a bopper?
Did you listen to like Bud Powell?

Oh sure. I mean in fact when they’d ask me questions, guys come to review the bands that I was with, they’d ask the guys individually, who’s your favorite piano player, and I’d say well I like Oscar Peterson and Erroll Garner, Erroll was my favorite. Because he was a friend of mine. He used to send me Christmas cards. And one day my son found a Christmas card in the drawer. He said, “hey Dad.” I said, “what?” “Erroll Garner?” I said, “what?” He says, “he sent you a Christmas card?” I said, “yeah I get one every year.” He said, “man!”
Wow, you’re legitimate all of a sudden.
He said, “I didn’t know you were that famous.” I said, “yeah, he’s my friend.” In fact he made a record of a thing called “That’s My Kick.” Did you ever hear it?

He’s got an introduction he must have been stoned when he did it because I don’t know how he did that [scats]. It’s like so erratic. I tried to notate it and I went crazy. I couldn’t do it. So I saw him on the street one day I said, “hey Erroll, please, I’m trying to write down that kick.” I said, “what did you do in that intro?” He says, “man, how am I supposed to know. Do you expect me to know that?”
Well sure and if you had been able to write it down and give it to him to play it, he couldn’t play it.
Oh of course not but he was great. In fact we did an album together. Go ahead, ask me something.
